title: PPT template gift: notes to a deck in the company's own template, inside the browser
plain: A web page takes a company PowerPoint template and a plain-text outline and gives back an editable deck in that template, and after it has loaded it cannot send anything anywhere.
what_why:
The page in docs/ loads Python (Pyodide, python-pptx and the deckfill package) from its own folder. It then adds a second Content Security Policy that blocks fetch, XHR, beacons, image requests and new workers. From then on, the user's template, outline and deck stay in the tab.

The deckfill package does the work in three calls the page makes one at a time:
- read: check the template's size and package graph, then sort its layouts into title, content, two, section and other
- plan: turn the outline into slides, choose a layout for each, and split slides the fit estimate says are too full
- fill: remove the template's sample slides, add the planned slides into the layouts' own boxes, copy footers the template shows, and put the template's own bytes back for every part the fill did not mean to change

The same package runs under CPython in the tests, and the browser's download is byte for byte the CPython output (C10).
requirements: D1: static site in docs/, Python through self-hosted Pyodide on the main thread, one deckfill module with read_template, parse_outline, plan_deck, fill
D1b: the template is untrusted: 50 MB file, 2,000 members, 300 MB uncompressed, 30 MB XML, 5 MB per XML part, 100:1 ratio, caps enforced on bytes actually read; safe XML parsing
D3: layouts classed by type and placeholders, never by name; a slide may only use a layout with a destination for every need
D4: sample slides removed with everything only they reach; every other part kept; footers follow what the template already shows; no text outside a placeholder
D5: split, warned or marked 'check this slide' by a fit estimate
D6: no request to another origin; at ready the page locks the network off, and Python's fetches are covered
D8: Cantonese copy in one file; mentron.hk look; phone view explains and hands over the link

design.text: Three layers. The page (docs/app.js) owns the UI, the loading and the lockdown. It calls a small Python bridge (deckfill.web.Session) that turns each step into JSON. The deckfill package reads, plans and fills. Python runs on the main thread, because GitHub Pages cannot give a worker its own policy and a worker made from a URL does not inherit the page's lockdown. The page paints a working state and yields before every Python call, and the D1b caps bound the longest call.

decisions.decision: Kept parts go back as the template's own bytes when their meaning is unchanged
decisions.why: G0 showed python-pptx re-sorting relationships and relativising absolute targets on every real template (EDB, elderly.gov.hk, Microsoft, USC), which C3 flagged; fixtures made by python-pptx never showed it

decisions.decision: The restore step compares libxml2 serialisations, not C14N 2.0
decisions.why: C14N 2.0 in lxml is pure Python: a 5.6 s main-thread task on the elderly.gov.hk template against C12's 3 s bar; now 1.55 s

decisions.decision: Lockdown is a second CSP meta added at ready
decisions.why: D6; measured in Chromium: after it, fetch from JS and Python and new workers are blocked and the server sees nothing (qa/e2e/c9-report.json)

implementation.title: The page loads Python from its own folder, then locks the network
implementation.text: loadEngine imports pyodide.mjs from docs/vendor, with indexURL and packageBaseUrl both set to that folder, so Pyodide's default CDN is never used. It loads lxml, Pillow and the vendored wheels, and unpacks deckfill.zip, which scripts/build_docs.py builds from src/deckfill ([build](scripts/build_docs.py#L15-L22)). Then it imports every module it will need and waits for the three font families, which scripts/build_fonts.py subsets and self-hosts ([fonts](scripts/build_fonts.py#L39-L50)). Only then does it call lockdown, which appends a meta policy with connect-src 'none', img-src data: blob: and worker-src 'none'. The #e2e hook exposes the Pyodide handle to the test only when the URL hash asks for it.

implementation.title: Read: caps first, then integrity, then classes
implementation.text: read_template runs package.load. unzip refuses too_big from the central directory before reading, and again on bytes actually read ([caps](src/deckfill/package.py#L79-L100)). Every XML part is parsed by xmlsafe.parse: entities, network and huge trees are off, and any DOCTYPE is bad_file ([parser](src/deckfill/xmlsafe.py#L25-L46)). check_integrity requires every relationship attribute to name a relationship and every internal target to exist ([integrity](src/deckfill/package.py#L234-L272)). Failures are DeckfillError codes the page maps to Cantonese messages ([errors](src/deckfill/errors.py#L1-L22)). classify then sorts each layout by its type attribute when the placeholders agree with it, and otherwise by its placeholders. A title placeholder is required, so HKUST template 15, whose titles are body placeholders, is refused as no_text_layout.

implementation.title: Plan: a compatible layout per slide, then splits by the fit estimate
implementation.text: parse_outline turns the D2 format into slides and warnings for lines it cannot place ([parser](src/deckfill/outline.py#L63-L80)). For each outline slide, plan_deck lists every layout with a destination for each of the slide's needs. It takes the user's override or the default, and refuses a layout without a destination. Each body's items go through chunk, which breaks between level-1 groups at 6 groups or when the height estimate passes the box. A group that alone overflows sets a fit warning, and a box the estimate cannot model sets 'check'. Continuation slides get （續） or (cont.).

implementation.title: Fill: sample slides out, with everything that pointed at them
implementation.text: remove_slides empties the slide list and drops custom shows and the section list. Then, in every kept part, it removes relationships to removed slides together with the elements that used them, such as a layout hyperlink to a sample slide. python-pptx then drops parts only those slides reached. The fill loop adds each planned slide from its layout, writes the title and bodies into the layout's own placeholders, removes the ones left empty, and appends footers chosen by footers_for, with each slide's own number written into slide-number fields ([loop](src/deckfill/fill.py#L286-L310)).

implementation.title: Fill: the template's own bytes go back for unchanged parts
implementation.text: python-pptx re-serialises every part it saves. _restore_kept compares each output part with the input's. For .rels it compares the resolved relationship sets; for XML it compares libxml2 serialisations of both parsed trees. When they mean the same, the input's bytes go back. It never touches the parts the fill is meant to change: the presentation part and its relationships, [Content_Types].xml, docProps/app.xml, and slide and notes parts. Then the output is zipped again and must pass the same integrity check as the input.

implementation.title: Download: bytes to a blob, no request
implementation.text: Session.fill returns the deck's bytes ([bridge](src/deckfill/web.py#L27-L81)). The page copies them out of Python, wraps them in a Blob and clicks a temporary anchor whose download name is the deck title, made safe for Windows by file_name. The working overlay is painted before the call and hidden after it. The session log shows no request after ready across two fills, a reset, 30 s idle and an offline fill.

check: C5 validator part NOT RUN: the Open XML SDK is not installed. qa/c5/run_validator.py runs it on every output beside its input once tools/dotnet exists.
G0 is 4 of 5 clean on every part except the validator. HKUST template 15 is refused by D3 step 5 as written.
C12 warm second visit is 5.0 s against a 5 s bar. The headless test profile does not keep the 9.6 MB wasm in its memory cache, so check it in real Chrome.
At the D1b worst case the wasm heap reaches 2.39 GB (qa/e2e/c12-report.json). Memory has no bar in the spec.
GitHub Pages MIME types for .wasm and .mjs are untested locally (deploy gate).
